title: Current Affairs One- Liner: 8th October 2026
excerpt: National: On 6 October 2026, the Union Cabinet approved two major initiatives: the creation of an Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) and a ₹10,000-crore SME Growth Fund. ITLA will function as an apex body for integrated transport planning, appraisal, monitoring and data analytics, while the SME Growth Fund will provide direct equity capital to scalable SMEs in manufacturing, services, technology and strategic sectors. On 6 October 2026, the Ministry of Rural Development notified 375 permissible works under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) [VB–G RAM G] Act, 2025. This is a 41% increase over the earlier 266 works. The new framework covers 128 water-security works, 111 core rural infrastructure works, 98 livelihood-related works and 38 works for disaster preparedness and extreme weather. In October 2026, Uttarakhand became India’s sixth fully literate state, joining Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim. The achievement is linked to literacy initiatives including ULLAS – New India Literacy Programme, which targets adults who missed formal schooling. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said the state will now focus more on digital literacy, financial literacy, health awareness and life skills. On 7 October 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi completed 25 consecutive years as head of government, beginning with his assumption of office as Chief Minister of Gujarat on 7 October 2001 and continuing as Prime Minister since 2014. The Union Cabinet passed a resolution marking the milestone, while several foreign leaders also sent congratulatory messages. On 8 October 2026, the Union Health Ministry is scheduled to launch JOSH or Joint Squad for Health Teams at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, to strengthen community participation in the TB Mukt Bharat campaign. In the first phase, JOSH Teams will operate across 55 districts in 11 states, bringing together Class-I officers, MY Bharat volunteers and NCC cadets for grassroots TB awareness and mobilisation. On 7 October 2026, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) released the Strategy for Environmental Economic Accounts in India 2026–2030. The five-year roadmap aims to measure natural wealth alongside conventional economic indicators, with priority areas including forests, water, land, soil, minerals, carbon stocks, biodiversity and pollination services. It succeeds the 2022–26 environmental-accounting strategy. On 7 October 2026, Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh became the state’s third cheetah habitat, after Kuno National Park and Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav released two Botswanan cheetahs, Vyom and Neera, into soft-release enclosures. It is also the first tiger reserve in India to receive African cheetahs under Project Cheetah. On 7 October 2026, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting notified the names of 13 journalist members of the Press Council of India, comprising six newspaper editors and seven other working journalists. The appointments are part of the reconstitution of the Council’s 15th term. The Press Council Act, 1978 provides for a Chairperson and 28 other members. On 6–7 October 2026, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs organised the National Conclave on Constitutional Rights and Legal Provisions for Tribal Communities at Scope Complex, New Delhi. Inaugurated by Union Minister Jual Oram, it brought together more than 75 delegates from around 30 states and UTs to discuss constitutional safeguards, documentation, grievance redressal, digitisation and implementation challenges faced by tribal communities. In October 2026, Command Hospital (Eastern Command), Kolkata successfully administered NexCAR19, India’s indigenous CAR-T cell therapy, to a 39-year-old serving soldier with relapsed/refractory B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia. NexCAR19 was developed through collaboration among IIT Bombay, Tata Memorial Centre and ImmunoACT and is intended to make advanced cell-based treatment for blood cancers more accessible in India. In October 2026, the West Bengal government moved towards introducing a Bill to rename the state Paschim Banga. The proposal has not yet become the official name. A state-renaming process requires legislative action and subsequent constitutional procedure involving the Centre and Parliament. The move revives a long-running debate over changing the name of West Bengal. On 6 October 2026, the University Grants Commission (UGC) issued a Letter of Intent to the University of Colorado Denver to establish a degree-granting campus in Hyderabad. It will become the first public American university authorised to establish such a location in India and the first foreign university in Telangana, with the first student cohort expected in August 2027. International: The 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) opened on 8 September 2026 at UN Headquarters in New York under the presidency of Khalilur Rahman. Its theme is Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar led India’s delegation during the High-Level Week and addressed the General Debate on 26 September. In October 2026, Egypt, Lebanon, Oman, Greece and Cyprus were reported to have expressed interest in joining the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC). The development was highlighted by French President’s Special Envoy for IMEC Gérard Mestrallet. IMEC seeks to build resilient transport, digital and energy links connecting India with the Middle East and Europe. Banking: On 7 October 2026, the Reserve Bank of India removed Paytm Payments Bank Limited (PPBL) from the list of scheduled banks following cancellation of its banking licence in April 2026. The removal means PPBL is no longer included in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act, 1934. Paytm’s UPI, QR, Soundbox and payment-gateway services operating through partner banks remain separate from PPBL. Economy: On 6 October 2026, the World Bank raised India’s real GDP growth forecast for FY2026-27 to 7.1% from 6.6% in its latest India Development Update. The upgrade reflects strong domestic demand, resilient exports and momentum in industry and services. The World Bank nevertheless flagged risks from high oil prices, El Niño-related disruption and volatility in international capital flows. In its October 2026 India Development Update, the World Bank identified India as one of the top 10 emerging-market performers in AI readiness. It highlighted India’s technical workforce, globally integrated IT sector and digital public infrastructure, while recommending broader AI adoption, better worker skills, stronger infrastructure and effective governance to spread the productivity gains of artificial intelligence. Science & Technology: In October 2026, a rare two-headed wolf snake was rescued from Dahod district, Gujarat. The non-venomous hatchling had two heads and four eyes due to bicephaly, a rare developmental abnormality. It was reported as the first such case in Gujarat and the fifth documented two-headed snake case in India, drawing attention from wildlife researchers and conservationists. In October 2026, Elon Musk-led Starlink said it had established 20 gateway sites in India equipped with hundreds of antennas as part of preparations for satellite internet services. The company has also developed India-specific security and data-localisation controls. Gateways connect satellite networks with terrestrial telecom infrastructure, particularly supporting connectivity in remote and underserved areas. Awards: In September 2026, Indian mathematician Mahesh Kakde of the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, was awarded the 2026 Ramanujan Prize for Young Mathematicians from Developing Countries. The prize recognised his contributions to algebraic number theory, including noncommutative Iwasawa theory and work on the Gross-Stark and Brumer-Stark conjectures. The prize is administered jointly by ICTP and the International Mathematical Union. Defence: On 6 October 2026, the Ministry of Defence signed a ₹661.50-crore contract with BrahMos Aerospace Private Limited for BrahMos Fire Control Systems and launchers for Indian Navy ships under the Buy (Indian-IDDM) category. The project has at least 68% indigenous content. BrahMos is the Navy’s principal surface-to-surface missile system for precision maritime strikes. On 6 October 2026, DRDO successfully flight-tested its indigenous High-Altitude Platform System (HAPS). The lighter-than-air platform reached 21 km above mean sea level and remained near 20 km for more than 30 minutes. Developed by ADRDE, Agra, HAPS is being designed for long-endurance stratospheric surveillance, intelligence gathering, communications and earth observation. On 6 October 2026, DRDO conducted the maiden live jump of the indigenous Advanced High-Altitude Parachute (AHAP) at Nyoma, Ladakh. The jump began at 16,000 feet, with parachute deployment at 15,500 feet and landing at 13,700 feet. Developed by ADRDE, AHAP is a static-line parachute designed for mass deployment of paratroopers in high-altitude terrain. In September 2026, GE Aerospace shipped four more F404-IN20 engines to Hindustan Aeronautics Limited for the LCA Tejas Mk-1A programme, taking cumulative deliveries to 14. The F404-IN20 is an afterburning turbofan engine powering the single-engine Tejas Mk-1A and is critical to HAL’s fighter-aircraft production schedule. On 6 October 2026, Pakistan test-fired an extended-range version of its indigenous Fatah-4 Ground-Launched Cruise Missile. The missile incorporates advanced avionics and navigation systems and is designed for low-altitude, precision conventional strikes. The test was presented by Pakistan as part of efforts to enhance indigenous long-range strike capabilities. On 6 October 2026, France conducted the first acceptance test of the upgraded M51.3 submarine-launched ballistic missile from the nuclear-powered ballistic-missile submarine Le Vigilant off Brittany. The missile carried no nuclear warhead during the test. The exercise validated the submarine’s strategic weapon system following maintenance and forms part of France’s modernisation of its sea-based nuclear deterrent. On 7 October 2026, Kochi-based EyeROV delivered two indigenous TROUT military-grade underwater Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs) to the Indian Navy, the first batch of a five-system order. The ROVs can operate at depths of up to 300 metres and are designed for underwater inspection, surveillance, reconnaissance, search, recovery and robotic intervention. In October 2026, Bharat Forge Limited secured a long-term contract from Pratt & Whitney Canada to manufacture and supply mission-critical aerospace engine components. Production will take place at Bharat Forge’s aerospace facility in India. The agreement strengthens India’s participation in global aerospace supply chains and supports expansion of domestic high-precision aerospace manufacturing capabilities. Military Exercise: On 7 October 2026, Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth inaugurated the 12th National Maritime Search and Rescue Exercise, SAREX-2026, organised by the Indian Coast Guard. The major sea demonstration was scheduled off Paradip, Odisha, on 8 October, with observers from 30 countries. The exercise simulates large-scale maritime emergencies and tests inter-agency search-and-rescue coordination. MoUs: On 6 October 2026, the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the Korean Sport & Olympic Committee (KSOC) signed an MoU during the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Signed by IOA President P. T. Usha and KSOC President Ryu Seung-min, it covers athlete and youth development, high-performance sport, coaching, sports science and good governance. On 7 October 2026, India and Ghana exchanged two MoUs covering scientific research, education and agriculture. One links the Zoological Survey of India with the University of Ghana for academic and scientific cooperation; the other connects ICAR with Ghana’s CSIR-Crops Research Institute for agricultural research, capacity building and technology transfer. Sports: On 6 October 2026, Serbia’s Novak Djokovic won his seventh China Open title in Beijing after Alex de Minaur retired during the final. It was Djokovic’s 102nd tour-level singles title and his first title of the 2026 season. He also became the first player to win at least one ATP title in 21 consecutive seasons. On 6 October 2026, Spain’s Carlos Alcaraz successfully defended his Japan Open title by defeating Czech player Jiří Lehečka 7-6(4), 6-4 in Tokyo. It was his second consecutive Japan Open crown and his first title after returning from a wrist injury. He became the first man since Pete Sampras in 1993–94 to win back-to-back Tokyo titles. In October 2026, the International Olympic Committee confirmed India among seven parties interested in hosting the 2036 Olympic Games. The other contenders include Qatar, South Africa, South Korea, Germany, Hungary and Türkiye. The prospective hosts will undergo the IOC’s dialogue and feasibility process before a final host decision in a later IOC vote. On 6 October 2026, the BCCI appointed Smriti Mandhana as the full-time captain of India’s women’s white-ball team, succeeding Harmanpreet Kaur. Mandhana had previously served as vice-captain and had already led India in 18 T20Is and four ODIs. She has also captained Royal Challengers Bengaluru to Women’s Premier League titles. Appointments: On 6 October 2026, the Government appointed Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff, in the rank of Air Chief Marshal, with effect from 31 October 2026. He succeeds Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh. Dixit was commissioned into the fighter stream in 1986 and was serving as Vice Chief of the Air Staff at the time of appointment. Summits & Conferences: Sagarmanthan 2026: The Great Oceans Dialogue is being held in New Delhi from 7–9 October 2026, bringing together more than 1,200 participants from nearly 75 countries. Co-hosted by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways and Observer Research Foundation, the third edition focuses on the theme Blue Geographies, New Aspirations: Trade, Technology, and Trust at Sea. Important Days: World Cotton Day was observed on 7 October 2026 to highlight cotton’s economic, social and environmental importance and its role in supporting millions of farmers and workers. The 2026 global celebration was held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, with the theme Cotton for Good: Building Prosperity Through Trade, Transformation and Partnership. Breast Cancer Awareness Month is observed throughout October every year to increase awareness about breast cancer, encourage early detection and screening, support patients and survivors and promote research. The campaign is internationally associated with the pink ribbon and emphasises that timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment can significantly improve survival outcomes. World Space Week 2026 was observed from 4 to 10 October. The annual UN-recognised celebration highlights the contribution of space science and technology to human development and encourages public interest in space education and innovation. The 2026 theme, Rocket Revolution, focuses on advances transforming access to and use of outer space. Indian Air Force Day 2026 was observed on 8 October, marking the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force, established on 8 October 1932. The 2026 theme is Indian Air Force – Infallible, Impervious and Precise, highlighting operational preparedness, resilience and precision in air operations. Obituaries: In October 2026, eminent Indian metallurgist and Padma Vibhushan awardee Palle Rama Rao passed away at the age of 89 in Hyderabad. He had served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Hyderabad, Secretary of the Department of Science and Technology, Chairman of the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, and Director of the Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory. On 6 October 2026, Oscar-winning American actress Eva Marie Saint passed away at the age of 102 in Los Angeles. She won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for her film debut in On the Waterfront (1954) and was also widely known for Alfred Hitchcock’s North by Northwest (1959). On 8 October 2026, veteran Indian actor Nana Patekar passed away at the age of 75 in Goa. Known for his work in Hindi and Marathi cinema, he earned national recognition for performances in films including Krantiveer, Parinda and Prahaar. His career was particularly noted for intense character roles and distinctive dialogue delivery. Questions: Q1. Q2. title: The skies have changed, so has IAF's mission: 94 years of India's air power
excerpt: Raised on 8 October 1932, the Indian Air Force began with four Westland Wapiti biplanes and five Indian pilots at Drigh Road, Karachi. Today it is the world's fourth-largest air force, operating fighters such as the Su-30MKI, Rafale and Tejas, though it fields around 29 fighter squadrons against a sanctioned 42. Its combat record spans the Second World War, the wars of 1947-48, 1965 and 1971, Kargil, Balakot and Operation Sindoor. The force is now evolving into a networked aerospace power, built around the Integrated Air Command and Control System, growing unmanned capabilities and long-range airlift. That reach extends to multinational exercises such as Tarang Shakti and humanitarian missions as far afield as Venezuela, underlining its expanding strategic role.

title: Abe Memorial corridor opens in Varanasi Rudraksh Centre: A friendship beyond protocol
excerpt: LUCKNOW: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Akie Abe, widow of former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, have unveiled the Abe Memorial Corridor at the Rudraksh International Convention Centre in Varanasi on Wednesday. The gallery is dedicated to a friendship the Chief Minister described as the living symbol of India and Japan’s historical, cultural and diplomatic ties. The inauguration fell on the date that marks twenty-five years since Narendra Modi first took the oath as Gujarat Chief Minister in 2001, the same milestone being observed across Uttar Pradesh this month as he marks twenty-five years in public life. A Friendship built on trust Addressing the ceremony, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the bond between Prime Minister Modi and Abe was built not on office but on trust, noting that positions changed over the years while the friendship endured. He called the corridor a tribute offered to Abe’s memory on behalf of Uttar Pradesh twenty-five crore residents, Prime Minister Modi and a hundred and forty crore Indians. Observing that Japan had once gifted Kashi its Rudraksh and Kashi was now embedding Japan’s former Prime Minister’s memory within that same Rudraksh. Read More: PM Modi at IMC 2026: 5G reaches every district as India accelerates digital transformation & mobile-enabled governance Two decades of a rare bond Tracing the friendship arc, the Chief Minister recalled that Modi and Abe first met in 2007, when Modi travelled to Japan as Gujarat’s Chief Minister. That same year, Abe told Indian Parliament that a strong India served Japan best interests, just as a strong Japan served India’s. The Kashi-Kyoto sister-city agreement followed in 2014 and in December 2015 Abe watched the Ganga Aarti alongside Modi during his Varanasi visit, laying the foundation for what would become the Rudraksh centre. The two leaders broke ground on India’s bullet train project in Ahmedabad in 2017 and Abe hosted Modi at his private residence in Yamanashi the following year. Padma Vibhushan and a final farewell The Chief Minister recalled that Abe was conferred the Padma Vibhushan, India’s second-highest civilian honour in 2021 and that Modi travelled to Tokyo in September 2022 to attend his state funeral after his assassination, with India observing national mourning. He reflected on how rare it is, in a world of transactional alliances, to find a friend who stands by you without weighing gain and loss. Beyond Rudraksh: An expanding partnership The Chief Minister used the occasion to outline the scale of Japan’s economic footprint in India, noting that nearly 1,400 Japanese companies currently operate in the country and that the partnership now extends into semiconductors, artificial intelligence, green hydrogen and critical minerals. He referred his own visit to Japan in February this year, during which agreements worth thousands of crores of rupees were signed with Japanese firms in Tokyo and Yamanashi. He recalled riding Japan’s Maglev train, capable of speeds exceeding 500 kilometres per hour and to study its precision engineering firsthand. Yamanashi prefecture is now Uttar Pradesh’s partner for green hydrogen energy, with a dedicated Yamanashi desk set up at Invest UP. A 500-Acre Japanese city near Noida The Chief Minister also announced that a 500-acre Japanese industrial city is being developed in the IEDA region near Noida International Airport, framing it as proof that Japan’s precision. Uttar Pradesh a market of twenty-five crore people, the country’s youngest workforce and its largest expressway and airport network, now complement each other. Looking to 2027, when India and Japan mark seventy-five years of diplomatic relations, he described the corridor as the first offering of that anniversary. It links Japan identity as the Land of the Rising Sun to Uttar Pradesh own as the Land of the Sun Dynasty through the state’s Buddhist circuit of Sarnath, Kushinagar, Kapilvastu, Shravasti, Kaushambi and Sankisa. Akie Abe’s Tribute Akie Abe grew visibly emotional recalling her husband, telling the gathering he had shared a deep personal bond with Modi and had spoken often of their 2015 Ganga Aarti together, a memory that left her wanting to visit Varanasi herself. She said her husband would have been overjoyed to see a memorial bearing his name, her eyes welling with tears as she spoke. She went on to praise the Rudraksh centre’s design, noting that its exterior carries 108 rudraksh beads, a number that similarly holds significance in Japan, where temple bells are rung 108 times to mark new beginnings. The Chief Minister presented her with a peacock crafted in Varanasi pink meenakari style as a memento. Cabinet minister Ravindra Jaiswal, Mayor Ashok Tiwari, Zila Panchayat chief Poonam Maurya, MLA Saurabh Srivastava and members of the visiting Japanese delegation were also present at the ceremony. For a city already woven through with monuments to friendship between the two nations, from the Japanese-funded Rudraksh centre itself to the twin-city pact with Kyoto. The new corridor adds a more personal register as a memorial less to a diplomatic relationship than to the two men who built it, meant, as the Chief Minister put to stand as a living classroom teaching the coming generation how far-sighted leadership can alter the shared future of two nations.

title: World Hindu Congress 2026: 60 countries, 4000 delegates & Hindu Expo; Hindu leaders unite for civilisational resurgence
excerpt: MUMBAI: As curtain raises for the largest confluence of the global Hindu community and for the biggest civilisational dialogue, World Hindu Congress(WHC), 2026 is set to attract more than 4000 delegates from 60 countries. Representatives from the global Hindu community who have accomplished remarkable heights in various strategically vital sectors such as business, media, education, academia, politics, culture, technology etc. are set to converge in Mumbai from December 10 to 20, to advance ideas, initiate strategic discussions and assure civilisational resurgence and prosperity. The theme of World Hindu Congress 2026 is “Samanam Vratam Saha Chittam – Shared Commitment, Collective Resolve”. The event will feature more than 45 sessions addressed by more than 150 speakers who are experts in diverse sectors such as education, academia, economy, politics, youth movement, tech world, culture, women empowerment, media, Hindu activism etc. The leaders will deliberate on ways and means for the future of Hindu society and its potential contribution to global prosperity. Most importantly, the WHC 2026, will provide a platform for the Hindu youth to connect, collaborate, exchange ideas and thereby script India’s growth story with civilisational renaissance. Addressing the press, Swami Vigyananand, Joint General Secretary of Vishwa Hindu Parishad(VHP) and Initiator of the World Hindu Congress(WHC) reiterated, “Hindu society is more visible and respected across the world than ever before, but this is not the time to rest. The World Hindu Congress is a strategic and structured movement to position Hindus globally in key areas of influence such as economy, education, media, politics. It provides a platform to connect, collaborate and contribute with a shared commitment & collective resolve”. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEKJcfBQyDQ Sarsanghchalak Dr Mohan Bhagwat, Chief Ministers & institutional experts to address Sarsanghchalak of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, Dr Mohan Bhagwat will address the inaugural session of the World Hindu Congress, 2026. Meanwhile, Chief Minister of Maharashtra Devendra Fadnavis, Chief Minister of Assam Himanta Biswa Sarma, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Mohan Yadav will address the World Hindu Congress. Other dignitaries including Vishal Chaturvedi, Director of Hanuman Ansh, Ashishkumar Chauhan, Managing Director & CEO of National Stock Exchange(NSE), Ashwini Bhide, Municipal Commissioner of BMC and MD of Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation are set to participate. Also, Prof. Abhay Karandikar, Member of NITI Aayog, Sanjeev Sanyal, Member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, Dr. Vivek Raghavan, Co-founder of Sarvam AI, Ajay Kumar Srivastava, MD & CEO of the Indian Overseas Bank and others will attend the largest Hindu gathering. Also Read: World Hindu Congress 2026: A strategic direction for Hindus to connect, collaborate & advance civilisational prosperity 4 plenary sessions on Dharma, Samaj, Vishwakarma & Bhasha The key pillars or core ideas of deliberation in the World Hindu Congress(WHC), 2026 includes Dharma, Samaj(Society), Bhasha(language) and Vishwakarma(Skill development). The Hindu leaders will ideate on how these forces can be a unifying factor among the Hindu community and aid civilisational resurgence or cultural revival. The Dharma plenary will bring together spiritual leaders representing diverse Dharmic traditions, sampradayas, spiritual institutions and philosophical schools from Bharat and other parts of the world, providing a platform for dialogue and exchange on the role of Dharma in contemporary society. Similarly, the Samaj plenary will focus on the social dimension of Hindu society and bring together experts from different communities, traditions and social institutions to deliberate on social cohesion, community development and the challenges before Hindu society. The Bhasha plenary will highlight the rich linguistic diversity of Hindu society, recognising the role of Bharat and the global Hindu community’s many languages in preserving civilisational knowledge, literature, traditions and cultural identity. Language is promoted as a unifying source, a tool for communication and to exchange civilisational wisdom, rather than a disruptive agency. The Vishwakarma plenary will focus on skill development, skilled workforce, entrepreneurship, innovation and the contribution of artisans, craftsmen and professionals to economic and social development. It will explore ways to strengthen the dignity of skilled workforce in Bharat and create greater global opportunities for the next generation. World Hindu Expo The unique and most noticeable feature of the World Hindu Congress, 2026 is the World Hindu Expo. The inaugural expo is aimed at stimulating trade and commerce and catalysing a new era of prosperity and economic growth for the Hindu society. It especially aims to provide opportunities to the youth to share ideas, collaborate on global scale and write India’s growth story. The World Hindu Congress held once every four years, has seven parallel conferences that showcases how the values, creativity and entrepreneurial spirit of the global Hindu community find expression in a variety of spheres, including economics, education, media, politics and other sectors. Interactive sessions offer space to deliberate the challenges and opportunities facing the Hindu community across the globe and aims to seek tangible solutions for the progress and prosperity of Hindus and the betterment of humanity as a whole. The inaugural WHC 2014 was held in Delhi, followed by WHC 2018 in Chicago and WHC 2023 in Bangkok.
